newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 11.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 11.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday:

* U.S. stocks rebounded on Thursday, with the Nasdaq index chalking up its sixth record close in a row as investors cheered upbeat corporate earnings. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended up 44.33 points at 7,886.76 after Wednesday's 120-point loss.
* On Thursday, the Jakarta Composite Index was down 8.99 points, or 1.22 percent, to 729.15 points after touching an intra-day low of 724.25 points on profit-taking, brokers said.
* On Friday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,434.00/35.00 at 0200 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,432.50/33.50.

* Small-capitalised metals firm PT Alumindo Light Metal Industries following a report that the International Finance Corporation, a World Bank unit, said it was backing loans totaling $35 million to fund expansion plans by the firm.
* Argo Pantes on a report that its wholly-owned subsidiary Argo Pantes Finance BV has completed a US$30 million floating rate notes issue due in 2000.

* Property firm Bakrieland Development on market talk that its holding company PT Bakrie Investindo will sell 60 million shares of it stake in the firm. Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper quoted sources as saying the firm would issue US$30 million exchangeable bonds by the end of July.
* Plastic and packaging sheets firm Dynaplast after Bisnis Indonesia daily quoted the company's director as saying it will split the nominal value of its stock and issue bonus shares.
* Electronics distribution firm PT Telagamas Pertiwi on a Jakarta Stock Exchange report on Friday that two founders of the firm had divested their stake by 2.72 percent and 2.61 percent.

* Texmaco units and might reap some market attention following a report in Bisnis Indonesia that a unit of the Texmaco group had acquired a majority stake in a synthetics unit of Hoechst AG. The newspaper quoted Texmaco chairman Marimutu Sinivasan as saying he would give details as soon as the deal was completed.
* Plantatation firms Bakrie Sumatra and London Sumatra after Indonesia revised the export tax structure for palm oil.
* Small-capitalised heavy equipment distributor Intraco Penta on reports it planned to form an alliance with a U.S. firm.
* Gajah Tunggal on reports the tyre manufacturer had told the stock exhange it planned to supply tyres to automotive firm PT Timor Putra Nasional.
* Property and banking stocks after the government announced measures to limit loans to the property sector.
